subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool top-up & overflow handling
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Park <sophie.park@atlashealth.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool top-up & overflow handling

Hi Sophie,

As we discussed on the call last week, your June renewal is a good opportunity to expand the dedicated pool to cover predictable growth and simplify operations during peak traffic. High level proposal:

- Add 20 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (new pool) for a 24-month term extension; staged provisioning over first 30 days.
- Throughput guarantee: aggregated baseline throughput of 800 requests/min for the pool (measured at our gateway, 95th latency target < 120ms for common 256-token requests).
- Overflow policy options (pick one):
  1) Soft overflow: automatic spill to hosted on-demand at agreed per-token rate + 10% premium; no request rejections.
  2) Hard cap: reject requests above reserved capacity; customer receives an error response and can retry against hosted.
  3) Hybrid: maintain a 2-GPU pre-warmed standby buffer billed as reserved but available within 10 minutes—overflow billed as per-minute active GPU-hours.

I attached a short model sizing sheet and a draft amendment that includes pricing tiers and an example billing calculation. Can you confirm which overflow model you prefer and whether procurement wants hourly billing vs per-token for overflow?

If this looks good, I’ll loop in Monica (CS) and Laura (Solutions) to lock in SLO language and the technical appendix.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
viv@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-amendment-draft.docx (attachment stub)

From: Sophie Park <sophie.park@atlashealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@atlashealth.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 20:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated pool top-up & overflow handling

Vivek,

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying questions from our side before we commit:

- Can you define the verification method for the "throughput guarantee"? Is that measured at the cluster egress (tokens/sec) or at request ingress? We need a reproducible test.
- For soft overflow pricing: do you bill per-token or per-GPU-minute? Our finance team prefers predictable per-hour charges rather than token-level variability.
- If we go hybrid with a pre-warmed buffer, what's the activation time SLA and is there an additional per-month standby fee?

Procurement also flagged that if we accept soft overflow, we need a ceiling on monthly overflow spend (e.g., auto-throttle if overflow spend > $X/month) or a manual approval step.

Looping Marco (DevOps) and procurement so they can raise any platform constraints.

Best,
Sophie Park
Director, ML Infrastructure | AtlasHealth
sophie.park@atlashealth.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Park <sophie.park@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated pool top-up & overflow handling

Sophie — thanks. Short answers and proposed contract language below. Monica and Laura are on for technical and ops details.

Verification method: we measure at the request ingress at the Redwood gateway (requests/min) with model family tagged. For contractual verification we run a joint throughput regression test (we provide a script) and capture p95 latency and sustained req/min over a 10-minute window.

Overflow billing options (proposed wording for amendment):
- Soft overflow (default): Redwood will route excess requests to Redwood Hosted. Overflow charges billed per 1,000 tokens at $0.XX + 10% premium. Monthly overflow charges will be capped at an agreed ceiling unless customer grants explicit approval.
- Hard cap (opt-in): Redwood will enforce a hard concurrency cap by returning a 429 when reserved capacity is exhausted. No overflow charges apply.
- Hybrid (recommended for AtlasHealth): Maintain a 2-GPU hot buffer billed as reserved capacity at $Y/GPU/month. Activation SLA: additional capacity provisioned and ready to serve within 10 minutes of trigger. Overflow beyond reserved+buffer billed as per-minute active GPU-hours (billed to nearest minute).

We can include an "auto-throttle" clause to pause overflow once monthly overflow spend reaches a procurement-defined threshold; that will be part of the amendment.

Monica/Laura — can you confirm the activation-time and the per-minute billing calc for the hybrid option? Ive attached the draft amendment to this thread for easy redlines.

-Vivek

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Park <sophie.park@atlashealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated pool top-up & overflow handling

Hi Sophie — quick technical detail and attachments to help procurement and DevOps decide.

Attachment summary:
- throughput_matrix.csv: measured req/min per GPU by model family and token length (CSV).
- overflow_pricing_v2.pdf: worked examples showing per-token vs per-minute billing across three traffic patterns.
- redwood-dedicated-amendment-draft.docx: draft contract language with the hybrid option and auto-throttle clause.

Key numbers from our lab:
- Baseline throughput (gpt-family-XL, 256 tokens): ~40 req/min per A100-equivalent GPU sustained at p95 latency <= 120ms.
- Warm buffer activation: pre-warmed instances are on standby capacity with model loaded; warm-to-ready time measured at 6-9 minutes (network variability accounted for). We guarantee <= 10 minutes in the amendment.
- Billing conversion example (hybrid): overflow 1 GPU-minute = $0.012 (example). We will show line items in the amendment so procurement can see worst-case scenarios.

Procurement note: if you prefer a flat per-hour standby fee instead of per-minute active billing, we can model that as an optional line item—happy to run numbers.

Monica Patel
Customer Success, Dedicated Accounts | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com

From: Sophie Park <sophie.park@atlashealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@atlashealth.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated pool top-up & overflow handling

Vivek / Monica — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. We reviewed the numbers with engineering and procurement. AtlasHealth is willing to proceed on the hybrid option with two adjustments before legal signs:

1) Billing unit for overflow: prefer per-hour active GPU charges (billed to the minute for accuracy but summarized as a per-hour rate on invoices) rather than token-level pricing. This greatly simplifies our chargebacks.
2) Auto-throttle cap: set default monthly overflow spend cap to $45,000 with an approval workflow to lift the cap for one-off incidents.

If you can update the amendment to reflect those two points and return a redline, procurement will run final internal approval and we can get DocuSign scheduled for the week of Jun 14.

Appreciate the help — we like the standby buffer approach and the activation SLA.

Best,
Sophie
Director, ML Infrastructure | AtlasHealth
